spec.goal: Build the two-day program of the conference from the talk submissions and the speakers' emails. Place every talk on the rooms x slots grid of one day, in its own track, with no room or speaker double-booked, every speaker available at their slot, every room big enough for its expected audience, and never two talks of one track at the same time. Honor the speakers' time preferences where possible, and write a short blurb per session.

root_goal.goal: Build the two-day program of the conference from the talk submissions and the speakers' emails. Place every talk on the rooms x slots grid of one day, in its own track, with no room or speaker double-booked, every speaker available at their slot, every room big enough for its expected audience, and never two talks of one track at the same time. Honor the speakers' time preferences where possible, and write a short blurb per session.

abstracts.abstract: This talk walks through how our team approached GPU scheduling over the past year. No prior experience is needed, but familiarity with the basics helps. We expect around 89 attendees.
abstracts.speaker: Kemi Silva
abstracts.title: Scaling GPU scheduling for small teams

abstracts.abstract: We share the mistakes we made with reward modelling and how we fixed them. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. Expected audience: about 70 participants.
abstracts.speaker: Chen Okafor
abstracts.title: Rethinking reward modelling

abstracts.abstract: This talk walks through how our team approached multi-agent planning over the past year. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. We expect around 104 attendees.
abstracts.speaker: Lars Iyer
abstracts.title: Multi-agent planning without the hype

abstracts.abstract: We share the mistakes we made with long-context attention and how we fixed them. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Last year a similar session drew roughly 54 people.
abstracts.speaker: Pablo Byrne
abstracts.title: Long-context attention: what actually worked

abstracts.abstract: This talk walks through how our team approached model distillation over the past year. No prior experience is needed, but familiarity with the basics helps. We expect around 39 attendees.
abstracts.speaker: Zoe Fischer
abstracts.title: Rethinking model distillation

abstracts.abstract: Why LLM evaluation harnesses is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Last year a similar session drew roughly 193 people.
abstracts.speaker: Ximena Silva
abstracts.title: Scaling LLM evaluation harnesses for small teams

abstracts.abstract: We share the mistakes we made with quantized inference and how we fixed them. No prior experience is needed, but familiarity with the basics helps. Expected audience: about 30 participants.
abstracts.speaker: Elif Fischer
abstracts.title: Scaling quantized inference for small teams

abstracts.abstract: A hands-on look at prompt caching, with code and real measurements. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. We expect around 35 attendees.
abstracts.speaker: Pablo Haddad
abstracts.title: Rethinking prompt caching

abstracts.abstract: We share the mistakes we made with dark patterns and how we fixed them. No prior experience is needed, but familiarity with the basics helps. We expect around 102 attendees.
abstracts.speaker: Zoe Fischer
abstracts.title: Lessons from dark patterns in production

abstracts.abstract: Why trust in AI assistants is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 59 people.
abstracts.speaker: Lars Sato
abstracts.title: A practical guide to trust in AI assistants

abstracts.abstract: This talk walks through how our team approached visualizing uncertainty over the past year. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 56 people.

abstracts.abstract: A hands-on look at usability testing at scale, with code and real measurements. No prior experience is needed, but familiarity with the basics helps. We expect around 63 attendees.
abstracts.speaker: Greta Haddad
abstracts.title: A practical guide to usability testing at scale

abstracts.abstract: A hands-on look at explainable recommendations, with code and real measurements. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. Expected audience: about 48 participants.

abstracts.title: Lessons from usability testing at scale in production
